scenarios.setting: You're interviewing for a position you really want. The manager begins the interview.

steps.speaker: Gerente
steps.es: Cuénteme un poco sobre su experiencia.
steps.en: Tell me a bit about your experience.

options.es: Tengo cinco años trabajando con computadoras.
options.en: I have five years working with computers.
options.feedback: Concrete and confident. Leading with a clear fact makes a strong impression.
Too vague for an interview. Give specifics — years, skills, roles.
Don't undersell yourself out of the gate! Frame what you DO have positively.

steps.speaker: Gerente
steps.es: ¿Y cuáles diría que son sus fortalezas?
steps.en: And what would you say your strengths are?

options.en: I'm organized and I learn fast.
options.feedback: Two clear strengths, stated plainly. Exactly what she's listening for.

options.en: I speak several languages, including Spanish.
options.feedback: Great — and saying it IN Spanish proves it. Strong move.

options.es: No sé, supongo que soy normal.
options.en: I don't know, I guess I'm average.
options.feedback: An interview is the time to shine, not shrink. Name a real strength with confidence.

steps.speaker: Gerente
steps.es: ¿Por qué quiere trabajar con nosotros?
steps.en: Why do you want to work with us?

options.es: Porque creo que puedo aportar mucho aquí.
options.en: Because I believe I can contribute a lot here.
options.feedback: Focuses on what you'll give, not just get. That's what managers want to hear.
Honest, but it's all about you. Show interest in what you'd bring to them.

options.es: Me interesa mucho lo que hace la empresa.
options.en: I'm very interested in what the company does.
options.feedback: Shows genuine interest in them specifically. A solid, professional answer.

steps.speaker: Gerente
steps.es: Muy bien. ¿Cuándo podría empezar?
steps.en: Very good. When could you start?

options.en: I can start whenever you need.
options.feedback: Flexible and eager — a great closing note that signals real availability.

options.en: I'd have to think about it.
options.feedback: Reasonable if true, but at the offer stage, hesitation can cool their interest.
Leading with money before an offer comes off poorly. Save salary talk for later.

scenarios.title: Meeting someone special
scenarios.setting: At a party, you're talking with Lucía, someone you've just met and really like. The conversation is going well.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Me cae bien hablar con vos. Sos diferente.
steps.en: I like talking with you. You're different.

options.es: A mí también me gusta hablar con vos.
options.en: I like talking with you too.
options.feedback: Warm and reciprocal — returning the feeling keeps the spark alive without overdoing it.
Lukewarm! She opened up a little — meet her warmth, don't deflect it.
Playful and a little flirty — works if your tone is light, risky if she meant it sincerely.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Bueno bueno, jaja. Contame más de vos.
steps.en: Good good, haha. Tell me more about you.

options.es: Vine a aprender español, pero me quedé por la gente.
options.en: I came to learn Spanish, but I stayed for the people.
options.feedback: Lovely and a little charming — it hints she's part of why you'd stay. Smooth.
Closes the door she's opening. Give her something — curiosity is interest.

options.en: What do you want to know?
options.feedback: Fine, turns it back to her — but offering something yourself first feels warmer.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Qué lindo. ¿Y te hallás aquí entonces?
steps.en: How sweet. So you feel at home here?

options.es: Cada día más, sobre todo esta noche.
options.feedback: Gently flirtatious without being too much — 'especially tonight' lands beautifully.

options.es: Sí, la gente es muy cálida.
options.en: Yes, the people are very warm.
options.feedback: Sincere and kind. A safe, genuine answer that compliments her world.
A bit flat for such a warm moment. Let a little more feeling through.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Me gustaría verte otra vez.
steps.en: I'd like to see you again.

options.es: Ojalá que sí. ¿Te doy mi número?
options.en: I hope so. Can I give you my number?
options.feedback: 'Ojalá' (subjunctive of hope) plus a clear next step — perfect, and confident.
'Me encantaría' (I'd love to) is warm and eager in just the right measure.
After such a sweet moment, 'maybe' is cold. If you're interested, show it!

scenarios.title: Saying how you feel
scenarios.setting: You and Lucía have been together a while. It's a quiet, tender moment, and you want to tell her what she means to you.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Estás muy callado. ¿En qué pensás?
steps.en: You're very quiet. What are you thinking about?

options.es: En lo feliz que soy con vos.
options.en: About how happy I am with you.
options.feedback: Open and warm — sharing the happy thought invites closeness. Perfect.
A missed chance to connect. She's inviting you in — step through the door.
Simple and intimate. 'En nosotros' says a lot in two words.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: ¿Ah sí? ¿Y qué pensás de nosotros?
steps.en: Oh yeah? And what do you think about us?

options.es: Que te quiero más cada día.
options.en: That I care for you more each day.
options.feedback: 'Te quiero' for tender affection — exactly the right register here. Lovely.
Way too lukewarm for the moment! She's opening her heart — meet her there.

options.es: Que sos muy importante para mí.
options.en: That you're very important to me.
options.feedback: Sincere and heartfelt. A beautiful thing to say and easy to mean.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Vos también sos todo para mí.
steps.en: You're everything to me too.

options.es: Quiero que sepás que te amo.
options.en: I want you to know that I love you.
options.feedback: The subjunctive 'que sepás' plus 'te amo' — the deepest declaration. Brave and beautiful.
'Same' to 'you're everything to me'?! This moment deserves your real words.

options.es: Me hacés muy feliz, de verdad.
options.en: You make me very happy, truly.
options.feedback: Heartfelt and genuine. 'De verdad' adds sincerity. Wonderful.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Yo también te amo. Con toda el alma.
steps.en: I love you too. With all my soul.

options.es: Ojalá siempre estemos así de bien.
options.en: I hope we're always this good together.
options.feedback: 'Ojalá... estemos' — subjunctive of hope, the perfect tender wish. Masterful.
'Mi amor' is the natural term of endearment — sweet and fitting.
Don't shut down the most tender moment! Let it breathe.

scenarios.title: Meeting the family
scenarios.setting: Lucía has brought you home to meet her parents for the first time. Her mother opens the door.

steps.speaker: Doña Marta
steps.es: ¡Pase! Así que usted es el famoso novio.
steps.en: Come in! So you're the famous boyfriend.

options.es: Mucho gusto, doña. Le traje estas flores.
options.en: Nice to meet you, ma'am. I brought you these flowers.
options.feedback: Respectful 'doña' plus a thoughtful gift — a flawless first impression here.
Far too casual for meeting a partner's mother. Warmth and respect matter enormously.

options.en: The very one. Nice to meet you, ma'am.
options.feedback: Charming and polite — playing along with her warmth while staying respectful.

steps.speaker: Doña Marta
steps.es: Qué detalle. Pase, pase, la comida está lista.
steps.en: How thoughtful. Come in, come in, the food is ready.

options.en: It smells delicious. Thank you for having me.
options.feedback: Praising the food and thanking her for the welcome — exactly right. She'll glow.
She cooked to welcome you! Declining the meal would be a real misstep here.
Curiosity is fine, but lead with gratitude for the welcome first.

steps.speaker: Don Pedro
steps.es: Así que usted hace feliz a mi hija.
steps.en: So you're the one who makes my daughter happy.

options.es: Hago todo lo posible, don Pedro.
options.en: I do everything I can, Don Pedro.
options.feedback: Humble, sincere, and using his name respectfully. A father wants to hear exactly this.
Honest and modest — shows you take it seriously without overpromising.

options.es: Pues obvio, soy lo mejor que le pasó.
options.en: Well obviously, I'm the best thing that happened to her.
options.feedback: Cocky with her father?! That's a fast way to lose his respect. Stay humble.

steps.speaker: Doña Marta
steps.es: Espero que se sienta como en su casa, mijo.
steps.en: I hope you feel at home, dear.

options.es: Ya me siento así. Se lo agradezco mucho.
options.en: I already do. I appreciate it so much.
options.feedback: Warm, grateful, and it honors her kindness. She just called you 'mijo' — you're in.

options.en: Thank you, ma'am. You're all very kind.
options.feedback: Gracious and respectful — acknowledging the whole family's warmth is a lovely touch.
Cold and guarded when she's embracing you. Receive the warmth openly.

scenarios.title: A vulnerable moment
scenarios.setting: Something has been weighing on you. Lucía senses it and gently asks. This is a chance to be honest.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Te conozco. Algo te pasa. Contame.
steps.en: I know you. Something's wrong. Tell me.

options.es: Es difícil de decir, pero quiero ser sincero.
options.en: It's hard to say, but I want to be honest.
options.feedback: Naming that it's hard AND choosing honesty anyway — that's real vulnerability. Beautiful.
We all hide this way, but she sees through it. Trust is built by letting her in.

options.en: I don't want to talk about it.
options.feedback: A valid boundary — but she's offering safety. Consider opening the door a little.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Tranquilo. Tomate tu tiempo. Te escucho.
steps.en: Easy. Take your time. I'm listening.

options.es: A veces tengo miedo de no ser suficiente para vos.
options.en: Sometimes I'm afraid I'm not enough for you.
options.feedback: Deeply honest — naming a fear like this is the bravest kind of trust. Real intimacy.
A safer deflection — but she's made space for the real thing. You can go deeper.

options.en: Forget it, I'll get over it.
options.feedback: Brushing her off after she made space can hurt. She wants to be there for you.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Mi amor, para mí sos más que suficiente.
steps.en: My love, to me you are more than enough.

options.en: Thank you for listening without judging.
options.feedback: Acknowledging her gift of listening deepens the bond. Tender and grateful.

options.en: It's hard for me to believe, but thank you.
options.feedback: Honest about the struggle while receiving her love — that's authentic, not negative.
Dismissive of her reassurance. She means it — let it land.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Quiero que sepas que siempre voy a estar.
steps.en: I want you to know I'll always be here.

options.es: Eso significa todo para mí. Te amo.
options.en: That means everything to me. I love you.
options.feedback: The perfect response to being chosen and reassured — open, loving, complete.

options.es: Yo también voy a estar para vos, siempre.
options.en: I'll always be here for you too, always.
options.feedback: Returning the promise makes it mutual. This is what partnership sounds like.
Understandable if you're guarded, but it doubts her sincerity. She means it — trust it.

scenarios.title: Making up after a fight
scenarios.desc: Repair things with someone you love
scenarios.setting: You and Lucía argued earlier and said things you regret. You've cooled down and come to make peace.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Pensé que necesitabas espacio.
steps.en: I thought you needed space.

options.es: Lo necesitaba, pero ahora quiero hablar.
options.en: I did, but now I want to talk.
options.feedback: Honest and constructive — acknowledging the space while choosing to reconnect. Mature.
Clear, warm intent. Leading with repair sets the right tone immediately.
Coming in still hostile won't repair anything. Cool down fully before you talk.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Yo también dije cosas que no sentía.
steps.en: I said things I didn't mean too.

options.es: Perdoná lo que dije. Estaba molesto, no pensé.
options.en: Forgive what I said. I was upset, I didn't think.
options.feedback: Owning your part without excuses is the heart of a real apology. Strong.
Assigning blame reopens the fight. Repair means owning your side, not scoring points.

options.es: Los dos nos pasamos un poco.
options.en: We both went a little too far.
options.feedback: Fair, though owning your own part specifically lands warmer than splitting it evenly.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: No me gusta pelear con vos.
steps.en: I don't like fighting with you.

options.es: A mí tampoco. Quiero que entendás cómo me sentí.
options.en: Me neither. I want you to understand how I felt.
options.feedback: Agreeing AND gently asking to be understood — that's how you grow from a fight.
Simple and warm. A shared commitment to do better.

options.es: Pues entonces no hagás esas cosas.
options.feedback: Turning it into a demand reignites it. Speak from your feelings, not ultimatums.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Vení aquí. Te quiero, tonto.
steps.en: Come here. I love you, silly.

options.es: Yo también te quiero. Perdón otra vez.
options.en: I love you too. Sorry again.
options.feedback: Warm, affectionate, and humble — the perfect way to close the loop and reconnect.
Tender and real — admitting you missed her even after a few hours is sweet.

options.es: Está bien, pero la próxima portate mejor.
options.en: Fine, but behave better next time.
options.feedback: A jab in the middle of making up undoes it. Just receive the affection.

scenarios.title: Talking like a local
scenarios.setting: You run into Roberto on the street. He greets you in full casual Nica mode.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: ¡Ey, maje! ¿Qué te contás?
steps.en: Hey, dude! What's up with you?

options.feedback: Perfect register — 'maje' back at him plus the casual 'aquí nomás.' You sound local.

options.en: I'm fine, thank you. How are you?
options.feedback: Way too formal with a buddy! 'Usted' with Roberto sounds stiff and distant here.
'En la lucha' (in the struggle/grind) is a great casual answer. Very natural.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Fijate que hoy hay juntada donde Beto. ¿Te apuntás?
steps.en: So there's a get-together at Beto's today. You in?

options.feedback: 'Dale pues' is the ideal casual yes, and you got the practical detail. Smooth.
Careful — to a Nica ear 'ahí veo' often signals a soft no. If you mean yes, say it!

options.es: Sí, me gustaría asistir al evento.
options.en: Yes, I'd like to attend the event.
options.feedback: Grammatically perfect but stiff — 'asistir al evento' for a house party sounds like a textbook.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: ¡Tuani! Va a estar deacachimba la cosa.
steps.en: Awesome! It's gonna be a great time.

options.en: Great! I'll be there for sure.
options.feedback: Enthusiastic and natural. 'Sin falta' (without fail) shows you're committed.

options.en: How nice that it'll be fun.
options.feedback: A little flat next to his energy. Match his vibe — get hyped!
Kind of a downer when he's hyping it up. Read the energy and roll with it.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: De show, maje. Nos vemos al rato.
steps.en: Cool, dude. See you in a bit.

options.en: See you there, dude. Take care.
options.feedback: Casual, warm, perfectly matched to him. You closed it like a true compa.

options.es: Hasta luego, que tenga buen día.
options.feedback: Polite but formal again — with Roberto, keep it loose: 'nos vemos, maje.'
Easy and natural — 'al rato pues' is exactly how friends sign off here.

scenarios.title: Getting teased
scenarios.desc: Give as good as you get
scenarios.setting: You're hanging out with friends and Roberto starts ribbing you, Nica-style. Teasing means they like you — so tease back.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Maje, con ese acento todavía parecés gringo perdido.
steps.en: Dude, with that accent you still sound like a lost gringo.

options.es: Y vos con esa panza ya sos dos majes.
options.en: And you with that belly are already two dudes.
options.feedback: Perfect — you teased right back. That's exactly how you earn respect here.
Taking it personally kills the fun. Among friends, teasing is affection — roll with it.

options.en: Haha, at least I learned, right?
options.feedback: Good-natured and fine — though firing back a joke would land even better.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: ¡Uy! El chele salió respondón.
steps.en: Whoa! The foreigner came back with a comeback.

options.es: Aprendí del mejor... digo, del más hablador.
options.en: I learned from the best... I mean, the most talkative.
options.feedback: Quick, playful, with a little twist at the end — that's real Nica banter. Excellent.

options.en: Of course, I can hold my own now.
options.feedback: Confident and casual. Shows you're comfortable in the back-and-forth.
It's not a fight! Misreading friendly teasing as conflict puts a wall up. Keep it light.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Jajaja, ya te volviste bien vacilón.
steps.en: Hahaha, you've become a real jokester.

options.es: Ideay, algo se me pega de andar con vos.
options.en: Well, something rubs off hanging out with you.
options.feedback: 'Ideay' plus a playful jab — flawless. You're thinking in Nica now.
Sweet but a little earnest for the moment. The banter's still rolling — keep playing.

options.en: It's 'cause I have a good teacher.
options.feedback: Warm and clever — a compliment wrapped in a joke. Nicely done.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Ya sos de los nuestros, maje.
steps.en: You're one of us now, dude.

options.feedback: Confident and warm — 'ni se pregunta' is a great idiomatic flourish. You belong.

options.es: Me alegra escuchar eso, de verdad.
options.en: I'm glad to hear that, truly.
options.feedback: Sincere — a nice moment of real warmth after all the joking. Balanced perfectly.
A bit flat for such a warm thing to say. Let the moment land with more feeling.

scenarios.title: Reading between the lines
scenarios.setting: You invite an acquaintance to help you move on Saturday. Listen carefully to what he really means.

steps.speaker: Conocido
steps.es: ¿El sábado? Uy... fijate que ahí veo, maje.
steps.en: Saturday? Oof... well, I'll see, dude.

options.es: Tranquilo, si no podés no hay bronca.
options.en: No worries, if you can't, it's all good.
options.feedback: You read it right — 'ahí veo' is a soft no. Giving him an easy out is the gracious move.

options.es: ¡Genial, entonces contá conmigo que ahí estás!
options.en: Great, so count on it, you're in!
options.feedback: He was gently declining! Pushing past a soft no puts him in an awkward spot.

options.es: ¿Eso es un sí o un no?
options.en: Is that a yes or a no?
options.feedback: Direct — sometimes useful, but here it corners him. Reading the hint is smoother.

steps.speaker: Conocido
steps.es: Es que tengo un compromiso, creo. No estoy seguro.
steps.en: It's that I have a commitment, I think. I'm not sure.

options.es: No te preocupés, ya conseguiré quién me ayude.
options.en: Don't worry, I'll find someone to help.
options.feedback: Perfect — you let him off the hook without making him say no outright. Very culturally tuned.

options.es: Pero si no estás seguro, ¡entonces vení!
options.en: But if you're not sure, then come!
options.feedback: He's hedging on purpose to be polite. Don't trap him — that's the whole point of the hint.

options.en: Okay, let me know if you can.
options.feedback: Reasonable, though it gently keeps the pressure on. A clean release would be kinder.

steps.speaker: Conocido
steps.es: Sí, mejor así. Pero cualquier otra cosa, ahí estoy.
steps.en: Yeah, better that way. But anything else, I'm here.

options.es: Claro, maje. Para una birra siempre, ¿va?
options.en: Of course, dude. For a beer always, right?
options.feedback: You kept it warm and light — reading the room and keeping the friendship easy. Spot on.

options.es: Ya veo, solo no querías ayudar a mover.
options.en: I see, you just didn't want to help move.
options.feedback: Calling out the soft no embarrasses him. The unspoken deal is you both pretend. Let it be.

options.es: Va pues, gracias de todos modos.
options.feedback: Polite and fine, though a warmer note would keep the bond stronger.

steps.speaker: Conocido
steps.es: ¡De show! Ahí nos pegamos una birra, pues.
steps.en: Cool! We'll grab a beer then.

options.es: Dale pues, maje. Ahí nos vemos.
options.en: Sounds good, dude. See you around.
options.feedback: Easy, friendly close — no hard feelings on either side. You handled the whole dance perfectly.

options.es: Eso, pero la birra la pagás vos por no ayudarme.
options.en: Yeah, but you're buying the beer for not helping.
options.feedback: Playful if your tone's right — but it does poke at the thing you'd both agreed to drop.
Relaxed and warm. A clean, friendly wrap-up.

scenarios.title: At the juntada
scenarios.setting: You arrive at a house party full of Roberto's friends. The music's loud and everyone's in full casual mode.

steps.speaker: Beto
steps.es: ¡Ideay, chele! Pensábamos que ya no venías.
steps.en: Hey, foreigner! We thought you weren't coming.

options.es: ¡Aquí ando, pues! No me lo iba a perder.
options.en: Here I am! I wasn't gonna miss it.
options.feedback: Natural and warm — 'aquí ando, pues' is exactly the right casual energy.

options.en: Excuse my lateness, there was traffic.
options.feedback: A bit formal for a house party. Loosen up — nobody's clocking you here.
Flat. The party's lively — bring some of that energy in with you!

steps.speaker: Beto
steps.es: ¡Eso! Agarrá una birra. ¿Cómo va todo, maje?
steps.en: There you go! Grab a beer. How's everything, dude?

options.en: Everything's awesome, dude. What a great vibe!
options.feedback: Slang nailed — 'deacachimba' and complimenting the 'ambiente' fit perfectly.
Sounds like a business meeting! Match the party energy — keep it loose.
Easy and upbeat. Works great in the moment.

steps.speaker: Beto
steps.es: Más al rato ponemos música pa' bailar. ¿Le entrás?
steps.en: Later we'll put on music to dance. You in?

options.en: Of course! Even though I dance kinda clumsy, haha.
options.feedback: Game and self-deprecating — 'chambón' (clumsy) is great slang. They'll love it.

options.es: Le entro, pero me enseñás los pasos.
options.en: I'm in, but you teach me the moves.
options.feedback: Enthusiastic and inviting them to include you. Perfect party spirit.
Flat refusal at a party shuts the door. Even 'I'm bad but I'll try' keeps you in the fun.

steps.speaker: Beto
steps.es: ¡Jajaja, este chele es lo máximo! Ya sos de la familia.
steps.en: Hahaha, this foreigner is the best! You're family now.

options.es: ¡Eso, maje! Gracias por hacerme sentir así.
options.en: Yeah, dude! Thanks for making me feel that way.
options.feedback: Warm and genuine while keeping the casual tone. A perfect blend.
Beautiful — a little idiomatic wisdom dropped casually. That's fluency with heart.
Deflecting the warmth feels a bit cold. Just receive the love — they mean it.

scenarios.title: You sound like a local
scenarios.setting: At the market, a vendor who's never met you is surprised by how you speak.

steps.speaker: Vendedora
steps.es: Oiga, ¿y usted de qué parte es? Habla raro pero bonito.
steps.en: Say, where are you from? You talk funny but nice.

options.es: Soy gringo, pero ya medio pinolero, jaja.
options.en: I'm a gringo, but half-Nicaraguan now, haha.
options.feedback: Charming and self-aware — claiming 'pinolero' playfully will delight her.
You clearly do! Don't undersell yourself when someone's complimenting your Spanish.

options.es: De los Estados Unidos, pero vivo aquí.
options.en: From the US, but I live here.
options.feedback: Clear and warm. Mentioning you live here explains the local flavor in your speech.

steps.speaker: Vendedora
steps.es: ¡No me diga! Si habla igualito que nosotros.
steps.en: You don't say! You talk just like us.

options.es: Es que aprendí en la calle, con la gente.
options.en: It's because I learned in the street, with the people.
options.feedback: A lovely, true answer — it honors the people who taught you. She'll appreciate it.

options.en: Thanks, it's taken me a lot of effort.
options.feedback: Humble and honest. Acknowledging the work behind it is genuine and relatable.
Bragging deflates the warm moment. Humility wins hearts here, not boasting.

steps.speaker: Vendedora
steps.es: Qué lindo. ¿Y le gusta vivir en Nicaragua?
steps.en: How nice. And do you like living in Nicaragua?

options.es: Me enamoré del país y de su gente, doña.
options.en: I fell in love with the country and its people, ma'am.
options.feedback: Heartfelt and respectful — 'doña' plus genuine warmth. She'll remember you.

options.es: Sí, este lugar ya es mi hogar.
options.en: Yes, this place is my home now.
options.feedback: Simple and moving. 'Mi hogar' carries real weight after this whole journey.
Lukewarm after she's been so warm! If you love it, let her hear it.

steps.speaker: Vendedora
steps.es: Pues bienvenido, pinolero adoptado. Aquí tiene su casa.
steps.en: Well, welcome, adopted Nicaraguan. Here you have your home.

options.es: Gracias, doña. Eso significa todo para mí.
options.en: Thank you, ma'am. That means everything to me.
options.feedback: The perfect close to the whole journey — gratitude, warmth, belonging. Beautiful.

options.es: Qué amable. Me hace sentir en familia.
options.en: How kind. You make me feel like family.
options.feedback: Warm and genuine — naming the feeling of family lands beautifully.
A little abrupt for such a tender welcome. Let the moment breathe before you go.

scenarios.title: A deep conversation
scenarios.setting: Over coffee, a thoughtful friend asks you a big, open-ended question. This is about expressing ideas with nuance.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: ¿Vos creés que la gente cambia de verdad?
steps.en: Do you think people really change?

options.es: Creo que cambiamos, pero la esencia permanece.
options.en: I think we change, but the essence remains.
options.feedback: Nuanced and balanced — holding two ideas at once is exactly C1-level thought.
A one-word answer wastes a rich question. This is the level where you develop ideas.

options.es: Depende de la persona y las circunstancias.
options.en: It depends on the person and circumstances.
options.feedback: Thoughtful hedging — acknowledging complexity is sophisticated and honest.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Interesante. ¿Y vos, has cambiado mucho?
steps.en: Interesting. And you, have you changed a lot?

options.es: Más de lo que habría imaginado al llegar.
options.en: More than I would have imagined when I arrived.
options.feedback: Conditional perfect ('habría imaginado') used naturally — elegant and precise.
True but thin. At this level, reach for the texture behind the answer.

options.es: El idioma me transformó por dentro, no solo la lengua.
options.en: The language transformed me inside, not just my speech.
options.feedback: Beautiful and reflective — a genuinely C1 way to express depth.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: ¿En qué sentido te transformó?
steps.en: In what sense did it transform you?

options.es: Aprender a pensar distinto me hizo ver el mundo distinto.
options.en: Learning to think differently made me see the world differently.
options.feedback: Articulate cause-and-effect on an abstract idea. This is real eloquence.
Honest, but you can — push a little. Even 'it's hard to put in words, but...' invites you to try.

options.es: Me dio otra forma de ser yo mismo.
options.en: It gave me another way of being myself.
options.feedback: Poetic and precise — a lovely, layered thought delivered cleanly.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Qué manera tan linda de decirlo.
steps.en: What a beautiful way to put it.

options.es: Es que vos sacás lo mejor de mis pensamientos.
options.en: It's that you bring out the best in my thoughts.
options.feedback: Warm, gracious, and a little tender — closing an abstract talk on a human note. Perfect.

options.es: Gracias. Me gusta pensar en voz alta con vos.
options.en: Thanks. I like thinking out loud with you.
options.feedback: Sincere and natural — acknowledges the joy of the conversation itself.

options.en: Well, it's not a big deal.
options.feedback: Deflecting a genuine compliment dampens the moment. Receive it warmly.

scenarios.title: The hypothetical game
scenarios.setting: Friends are passing time with hypothetical questions. The skill: the past subjunctive and conditional, used smoothly.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Si pudieras vivir en cualquier época, ¿cuál sería?
steps.en: If you could live in any era, which would it be?

options.es: Si pudiera, escogería los años sesenta.
options.en: If I could, I'd choose the sixties.
options.feedback: Past subjunctive + conditional, paired perfectly ('pudiera' / 'escogería'). Flawless.
Answers it, but skips the grammar the game is built on. Frame it with 'si pudiera...'
Present tense breaks the hypothetical. This needs the conditional: 'viviría' or 'escogería'.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: ¡Buena! ¿Y si tuvieras que renunciar a un sentido?
steps.en: Nice! And if you had to give up one sense?

options.es: Si tuviera que hacerlo, renunciaría al olfato.
options.en: If I had to, I'd give up smell.
options.feedback: 'Si tuviera... renunciaría' — textbook-perfect hypothetical, delivered naturally.

options.en: I'd give up smell, I think.
options.feedback: Clean conditional with a natural hedge ('creo'). Works beautifully.

options.en: I don't want to give up anything.
options.feedback: Dodges the game — fine once, but the fun is in playing along with the hypothetical.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Jajaja. ¿Y si no hubieras venido a Nicaragua?
steps.en: Hahaha. And if you hadn't come to Nicaragua?

options.es: Si no hubiera venido, no sería quien soy hoy.
options.en: If I hadn't come, I wouldn't be who I am today.
options.feedback: Pluperfect subjunctive + conditional ('hubiera venido' / 'sería') — advanced and elegant.

options.es: Mi vida habría sido muy diferente.
options.en: My life would have been very different.
options.feedback: Conditional perfect ('habría sido') — sophisticated and exactly right.

options.en: I didn't come, but here I am.
options.feedback: Contradicts itself and drops the hypothetical. Use 'si no hubiera venido...'

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Qué profundo te pusiste, maje.
steps.en: You got deep, dude.

options.es: Vos preguntaste, yo solo respondí con el alma.
options.en: You asked, I just answered from the soul.
options.feedback: Playful yet sincere — a graceful register blend between the game and real feeling.

options.es: Es que tus preguntas dan para pensar.
options.en: It's that your questions give a lot to think about.
options.feedback: Natural and warm — turns the compliment back nicely.
No need to apologize for depth! Own the thoughtful moment.

scenarios.title: Holding a debate
scenarios.setting: In a work meeting, you disagree with a proposal. The skill: persuade with logic, concede gracefully, stay composed.

steps.speaker: Colega
steps.es: Deberíamos lanzar el producto ya. No hay tiempo que perder.
steps.en: We should launch the product now. No time to lose.

options.es: Entiendo la urgencia, pero hay riesgos que considerar.
options.en: I understand the urgency, but there are risks to consider.
options.feedback: Validates his point first, then pivots — the hallmark of persuasive disagreement.
Blunt contradiction shuts down dialogue. Acknowledge, then make your case.
If you actually disagree, caving isn't persuasion. Hold your ground respectfully.

steps.speaker: Colega
steps.es: ¿Qué riesgos? El mercado está listo ahora.
steps.en: What risks? The market is ready now.

options.es: Concedo ese punto, sin embargo, las pruebas son incompletas.
options.en: I concede that point, however, the testing is incomplete.
options.feedback: 'Concedo... sin embargo' — conceding then countering is sophisticated debate structure.

options.es: El mercado no lo es todo.
options.feedback: A fair jab, but vague. Back it with the specific risk to be convincing.

options.en: I already told you, there are risks.
options.feedback: Repeating without evidence weakens you. Name the actual risk.

steps.speaker: Colega
steps.es: Bueno... ¿y qué propones entonces?
steps.en: Well... so what do you propose then?

options.es: Una prueba breve primero; así reducimos el riesgo sin perder tiempo.
options.en: A short test first; that way we cut risk without losing time.
options.feedback: Offering a solution that honors HIS concern (time) too — that's how you win a debate.
A position, but no bridge to his urgency. Give him something he can say yes to.

options.en: I don't know, but not like this.
options.feedback: Opposing without an alternative leaves you stuck. Always bring a proposal.

steps.speaker: Colega
steps.es: Mmm... eso sí podría funcionar.
steps.en: Hmm... that could actually work.

options.es: Me alegra que lo veamos parecido. Trabajemos en eso.
options.en: I'm glad we see it similarly. Let's work on that.
options.feedback: Gracious in winning — framing it as 'we' keeps the relationship strong. Masterful.
Gloating undoes the goodwill you just built. Win humbly.

options.en: Perfect, let's move forward together then.
options.feedback: Collaborative and forward-looking. A clean, professional close.

scenarios.title: Catching the irony
scenarios.desc: Read tone and respond in kind
scenarios.setting: You show up late, again. Roberto greets you with classic deadpan sarcasm. The skill: catch the irony and volley it back.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: ¡Pero qué puntual! Solo cuarenta minutos tarde.
steps.en: How punctual! Only forty minutes late.

options.es: Es que la puntualidad es lo mío, ya sabés.
options.en: Punctuality is my thing, you know.
options.feedback: You caught the sarcasm and played along — leaning INTO the joke is the witty move.

options.es: Perdón, de verdad lo siento mucho.
options.en: Sorry, I really am very sorry.
options.feedback: He's teasing, not scolding — earnest apology misreads the tone. Lighten up and volley back.
Defensiveness kills the joke. He's ribbing you affectionately — play, don't justify.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Ah, claro. Deberían darte un premio.
steps.en: Oh, sure. They should give you an award.

options.es: Ya lo tengo en casa, junto a los otros.
options.en: I've already got it at home, next to the others.
options.feedback: Brilliant — extending the bit with a deadpan add-on. That's native-level humor.

options.es: Jaja, sí, perdón por la tardanza.
options.en: Haha, yeah, sorry for being late.
options.feedback: The laugh shows you got it, but slipping into apology deflates the volley. Keep the bit going.
Calling out the exaggeration ends the game flatly. The fun is in escalating it together.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Jajaja, ya ni con vos se puede.
steps.en: Hahaha, can't even win with you anymore.

options.es: Aprendí del maestro del sarcasmo, ¿qué esperabas?
options.en: I learned from the master of sarcasm, what'd you expect?
options.feedback: A compliment wrapped in a comeback — peak Nica banter. You've fully arrived.

options.es: Tantos años de práctica con vos.
options.en: So many years of practice with you.
options.feedback: Warm, witty, and self-aware. The friendship and the humor both shine.
You can pivot, but cutting the fun short feels abrupt. Let the laugh land first.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Te volviste más nica que yo, maje.
steps.en: You've become more Nica than me, dude.

options.es: Alguien tenía que mantener el nivel por aquí.
options.en: Someone had to keep up the standard around here.
options.feedback: Cheeky and confident — capping the exchange on a perfect comedic high note.

options.es: Jaja, me lo tomo como un honor.
options.en: Haha, I'll take that as an honor.
options.feedback: Warm and genuine while staying playful — a lovely way to receive the praise.

options.es: Qué va, vos seguís siendo el rey.
options.feedback: Generous and humble with a wink — true camaraderie. Beautifully done.

scenarios.title: Speaking for a cause
scenarios.setting: At a community meeting about fixing the neighborhood park, you're asked to make the case. The skill: persuasive, eloquent advocacy.

steps.speaker: Vecino
steps.es: ¿Y por qué deberíamos gastar en ese parque viejo?
steps.en: And why should we spend on that old park?

options.es: Porque no es solo un parque; es el corazón del barrio.
options.en: Because it's not just a park; it's the heart of the neighborhood.
options.feedback: Reframing from cost to meaning — that's persuasive rhetoric. Opens hearts, not just minds.
Too thin to move anyone. Advocacy needs a vision, not just a complaint.

options.es: Porque nuestros hijos merecen un lugar seguro.
options.en: Because our children deserve a safe place.
options.feedback: Appeals to shared values — children, safety. Emotionally resonant and effective.

steps.speaker: Vecino
steps.es: Pero no tenemos dinero para eso.
steps.en: But we don't have money for that.

options.es: Si nos organizamos, juntos podemos lograr más de lo que creemos.
options.en: If we organize, together we can achieve more than we think.
options.feedback: Conditional 'si nos organizamos' plus a hopeful vision — rallying language at its best.
Dismissing a real concern alienates people. Address it, don't belittle it.

options.es: Podemos pedir ayuda y aportar entre todos.
options.en: We can ask for help and all chip in.
options.feedback: Concrete and inclusive — turns an objection into a shared plan. Smart advocacy.

steps.speaker: Vecino
steps.es: Suena bonito, pero ¿de verdad cambiaría algo?
steps.en: Sounds nice, but would it really change anything?

options.es: Un barrio que cuida sus espacios se cuida a sí mismo.
options.en: A neighborhood that cares for its spaces cares for itself.
options.feedback: Aphoristic and quotable — the kind of line that sticks in people's minds. Eloquent.

options.es: Tal vez no, pero hay que intentar.
options.en: Maybe not, but we have to try.
options.feedback: Honest, but it concedes too much ground. Lead with conviction, not doubt.

options.es: Imaginen a los niños jugando ahí de nuevo.
options.en: Imagine the children playing there again.
options.feedback: Painting a vivid picture is powerful persuasion — you make them feel the future.

steps.speaker: Vecino
steps.es: Bueno... el chele habla con razón. ¡Cuenten conmigo!
steps.en: Well... the foreigner makes sense. Count me in!

options.es: ¡Eso! Juntos vamos a recuperar lo nuestro.
options.en: Yes! Together we'll reclaim what's ours.
options.feedback: Rallying and unifying — 'lo nuestro' makes it collective. A rousing close.

options.en: Thank you. I knew you'd understand.
options.feedback: Gracious and affirming — credits them for coming around. Warm leadership.
Condescending — it insults everyone who hesitated. You just won them over; don't lose them now.

scenarios.title: Trading proverbs
scenarios.setting: Doña Marta is dispensing wisdom in proverbs, as grandmothers do. The skill: understand them and reply in kind.

steps.speaker: Doña Marta
steps.es: Acordate, mijo: camarón que se duerme, se lo lleva la corriente.
steps.en: Remember, dear: the shrimp that sleeps gets swept off by the current.

options.es: Cierto, doña. Al que madruga, Dios lo ayuda.
options.en: True, ma'am. God helps those who rise early.
options.feedback: You answered a proverb WITH a proverb on the same theme — that's true mastery. She'll be delighted.

options.en: What do shrimp have to do with it?
options.feedback: Taking a proverb literally misses its whole point. The image carries the meaning — read past the words.

options.es: Tiene razón, hay que estar atento.
options.en: You're right, one must stay alert.
options.feedback: You understood it — good. But matching her proverb with your own would really land.

steps.speaker: Doña Marta
steps.es: ¡Eso! Veo que ya tenés colmillo. ¿Y este: a buen entendedor...?
steps.en: There you go! I see you've got savvy. And this one: to a good listener...?

options.feedback: You completed the classic refrán perfectly — 'a buen entendedor, pocas palabras.' Flawless.
Reasonable guess, but the set ending is 'pocas palabras.' These are fixed — worth memorizing.
Honest! And fine — but this is among the most common refranes. Tuck it away.

steps.speaker: Doña Marta
steps.es: ¡Ay, este muchacho! Habla mejor que muchos de aquí.
steps.en: Oh, this young man! He speaks better than many from here.

options.es: Aprendí de las mejores, empezando por usted.
options.en: I learned from the best, starting with you.
options.feedback: Gracious and warm, with a little courtly charm — exactly the right note with an elder.

options.es: Es que tuve buenos maestros en la calle.
options.en: It's that I had good teachers in the street.
options.feedback: Humble and true — honoring the everyday people who taught you. Lovely.
Boasting deflates her compliment. Humility is the higher register here.

steps.speaker: Doña Marta
steps.es: Dios te bendiga, mijo. Sos de los nuestros.
steps.en: God bless you, dear. You're one of us.

options.es: Que Dios la bendiga a usted, doña. Gracias por todo.
options.en: May God bless you, ma'am. Thank you for everything.
options.feedback: Returning the blessing in kind is deeply respectful and culturally perfect. A beautiful close.

options.es: Eso es lo más lindo que me han dicho.
options.en: That's the loveliest thing anyone's said to me.
options.feedback: Heartfelt and sincere — receiving her blessing with real emotion. Touching.
Polite, but the moment deserves more warmth than a plain thanks.

scenarios.title: Discussing poetry
scenarios.setting: At a cultural evening, conversation turns to Rubén Darío. The skill: an elevated, literary register and genuine appreciation.

steps.speaker: Profesora
steps.es: ¿Ha leído usted a Darío? Es nuestro mayor poeta.
steps.en: Have you read Darío? He's our greatest poet.

options.es: Sí, su musicalidad me cautivó por completo.
options.en: Yes, his musicality captivated me completely.
options.feedback: 'Musicalidad' and 'cautivó' — precise literary vocabulary delivered naturally. Elegant.
True, but the register's too casual for a literary discussion. Reach for richer words.
Honest — and an invitation for her to share. But if you have read him, show that appreciation.

steps.speaker: Profesora
steps.es: ¿Y qué le evoca su poesía?
steps.en: And what does his poetry evoke for you?

options.es: Una nostalgia hermosa por lo que se va y no vuelve.
options.en: A beautiful nostalgia for what leaves and doesn't return.
options.feedback: Poetic and perceptive — you're discussing literature AS literature. Genuinely C2.

options.es: Me hace sentir cosas, no sé bien cómo decirlo.
options.en: It makes me feel things, I'm not sure how to say it.
options.feedback: Sincere, but at this level you CAN articulate it. Trust your vocabulary and reach.

options.es: Sobre todo, la belleza del idioma mismo.
options.en: Above all, the beauty of the language itself.
options.feedback: A thoughtful, layered answer — appreciating the language as its own art. Sophisticated.

steps.speaker: Profesora
steps.es: Me sorprende su sensibilidad. ¿De dónde es usted?
steps.en: Your sensitivity surprises me. Where are you from?

options.es: De fuera, aunque el español me adoptó hace tiempo.
options.en: From abroad, though Spanish adopted me long ago.
options.feedback: 'El español me adoptó' — a graceful, almost poetic way to put it. Beautiful turn of phrase.

options.es: Soy extranjero, pero amo esta lengua.
options.en: I'm a foreigner, but I love this language.
options.feedback: Sincere and warm, in fitting register. A lovely, honest answer.
Fine, but a touch flat after such a graceful question. Match her register with some warmth.

steps.speaker: Profesora
steps.es: Pues ama nuestra lengua más que muchos nativos.
steps.en: Well, you love our language more than many natives.

options.es: Quien llega de fuera a veces ve la belleza con ojos nuevos.
options.en: One who arrives from outside sometimes sees the beauty with fresh eyes.
options.feedback: Wise and quotable — an almost aphoristic reflection. This is the summit of expression.

options.es: Es un honor escuchar eso de usted.
options.en: It's an honor to hear that from you.
options.feedback: Gracious and appropriately humble in an elevated setting. Well judged.

options.en: Thanks, I do what I can.
options.feedback: Modest, but a bit plain for the eloquence she just praised. Let your range show.

scenarios.title: A battle of wits
scenarios.setting: Among close friends, a fast-paced game of puns and comebacks breaks out. The skill: think in layers and volley instantly.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Maje, vos sos como el café: mejor con leche y sin amargura.
steps.en: Dude, you're like coffee: better with milk and without bitterness.

options.es: Y vos como el azúcar: dulce pero malo en exceso.
options.en: And you're like sugar: sweet but bad in excess.
options.feedback: You extended his metaphor and flipped it back — that's high-level improvised wordplay. Brilliant.
Appreciating it is fine, but the game is to volley. Fire one back!
At this level you CAN get it — the milk/bitterness layering is the joke. Stay in the game.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: ¡Uy! Te las traés. A ver si seguís el ritmo.
steps.en: Whoa! You've got it in you. Let's see if you keep the pace.

options.es: Tranquilo, que el que ríe último, ríe mejor.
options.en: Relax, he who laughs last, laughs best.
options.feedback: Dropping a proverb mid-banter as a comeback — layered and witty. Native-level play.

options.en: Go on, throw what you've got.
options.feedback: Confident and casual — accepting the challenge with swagger. Perfect energy.
Bowing out early cuts the fun. You're holding your own — keep going!

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Este chele ya no se deja. ¡Está deacachimba!
steps.en: This foreigner doesn't back down anymore. He's awesome!

options.es: Es que con vos de rival, uno aprende a la fuerza.
options.en: It's that with you as a rival, one learns by force.
options.feedback: A compliment disguised as a jab — peak banter. You're thinking in two layers at once.

options.en: Years of putting up with you leave something, no?
options.feedback: Cheeky and affectionate — the perfect register among old friends. Effortless.
Too earnest for the moment — the bit's still flying. Keep playing!

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Jajaja, ya sos más nica que el gallo pinto, maje.
steps.en: Hahaha, you're more Nica than gallo pinto now, dude.

options.es: Y con más sabor, modestia aparte.
options.en: And with more flavor, modesty aside.
options.feedback: You extended the food metaphor with a wink — the comedic button on the whole exchange. Masterful.

options.es: No hay mayor honor que ese, hermano.
options.en: There's no greater honor than that, brother.
options.feedback: Warm sincerity landing after all the jokes — a perfect tonal shift to close on.
Ending it flatly wastes a great setup. Land one more line, then bask in it.

scenarios.title: Speaking with eloquence
scenarios.setting: At Roberto's wedding, you're unexpectedly asked to say a few words. The skill: rise to the occasion with warmth and eloquence.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Maje, decí unas palabras. Sos parte de la familia.
steps.en: Dude, say a few words. You're part of the family.

options.es: Será un honor. Denme un momento para hacerle justicia.
options.en: It'll be an honor. Give me a moment to do it justice.
options.feedback: Gracious and self-assured — buying a beat to speak well rather than blurting. Poised.

options.es: No, no, mejor que hable otro.
options.en: No, no, better someone else speaks.
options.feedback: Refusing the honor at a friend's wedding stings. You have the words now — rise to it.
Warm and willing. A simple, gracious yes that honors the invitation.

steps.speaker: Invitados
steps.es: ¡Que hable, que hable!
steps.en: Speech, speech!

options.es: Hace años llegué a esta tierra sin conocer a nadie.
options.en: Years ago I came to this land knowing no one.
options.feedback: Opening with your own story draws everyone in — a storyteller's instinct. Beautiful start.

options.es: Eh... pues... felicidades a los novios.
options.en: Uh... well... congrats to the couple.
options.feedback: Nerves are natural, but you can do better than filler. Take a breath and begin with heart.

options.es: Voy a ser breve porque hay comida esperando.
options.en: I'll be brief because there's food waiting.
options.feedback: A light joke can work, but at a wedding, lead with warmth before humor.

steps.speaker: Invitados
steps.es: (silencio atento)
steps.en: (attentive silence)

options.es: Roberto me dio su amistad, y con ella, un hogar.
options.en: Roberto gave me his friendship, and with it, a home.
options.feedback: A moving, well-built line — friendship to home is a gorgeous progression. The room is yours.

options.es: Son buenas personas y los quiero mucho.
options.en: They're good people and I love them a lot.
options.feedback: Sincere, but plain for a toast. This is the moment to let your eloquence shine.

options.es: Que vivan los novios y que sean felices.
options.en: Long live the couple, may they be happy.
options.feedback: A classic, heartfelt toast line — simple and traditional, lands warmly.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: (con lágrimas) Gracias, hermano. Sabía que dirías algo así.
steps.en: (tearfully) Thank you, brother. I knew you'd say something like that.

options.es: ¡Por los novios! Que su amor dure más que mis errores de español.
options.en: To the couple! May their love outlast my Spanish mistakes.
options.feedback: A toast that's heartfelt AND funny, with a humble callback to your journey. Absolutely perfect.

options.es: ¡Salud por una vida juntos llena de amor!
options.en: Cheers to a life together full of love!
options.feedback: A warm, classic toast that raises the glass beautifully. The room will cheer.
Undercutting a tender moment for a joke about food deflates it. Let the warmth crest first.

scenarios.title: They think you're a native
scenarios.setting: In a city where no one knows you, a stranger chats with you and simply assumes you were born here. The final test — and the payoff.

steps.speaker: Desconocido
steps.es: ¿Vos también sos de por aquí? Se nota el acento.
steps.en: Are you from around here too? I can tell by the accent.

options.en: I wear the accent well, don't I?
options.feedback: Playful and confident — letting the assumption ride with a wink. You've earned the smoothness.

options.es: Algo así. El corazón sí es de aquí.
options.en: Something like that. My heart, at least, is from here.
options.feedback: Poetic and warm — true without breaking the moment. A graceful, earned answer.
Perfectly honest — and a fine choice. But notice: he couldn't tell. That's the whole journey, right there.

steps.speaker: Desconocido
steps.es: ¡No me digás! Pues hablás igualito que nosotros.
steps.en: You don't say! Well, you talk just like us.

options.es: Es que esta tierra se me metió en el alma.
options.en: It's that this land got into my soul.
options.feedback: A line worthy of the moment — almost literary, deeply felt. This is C2 with heart.

options.es: Años de vivir, escuchar y querer este lugar.
options.en: Years of living, listening, and loving this place.
options.feedback: Beautifully balanced — the recipe for true fluency in one elegant sentence.

options.en: Yes, it took me a lot to achieve it.
options.feedback: True, but it centers the struggle over the joy. Let the wonder of arriving shine through.

steps.speaker: Desconocido
steps.es: Qué bonito. ¿Y nunca pensás en irte?
steps.en: How nice. And do you never think of leaving?

options.es: ¿Para qué irme, si ya encontré mi lugar en el mundo?
options.en: Why leave, if I already found my place in the world?
options.feedback: A rhetorical question delivered with quiet certainty — eloquent and moving. The summit.

options.es: Uno no deja el lugar que lo hizo quien es.
options.en: One doesn't leave the place that made them who they are.
options.feedback: Aphoristic and profound — the kind of line a native might say. You've fully arrived.

options.es: A veces, pero no en serio.
options.feedback: Honest, but it lets the air out of a soaring moment. Trust the depth you're capable of now.

steps.speaker: Desconocido
steps.es: Pues bienvenido a casa, paisano.
steps.en: Well, welcome home, countryman.

options.es: Gracias, paisano. No hay palabra más linda que 'casa'.
options.en: Thanks, countryman. There's no lovelier word than 'home'.
options.feedback: The perfect final note of the entire journey — being called 'paisano' and embracing 'casa.' Complete.
Quiet, earned, and deeply moving. After the whole road from 'buenas' — this is the destination.
A bit flat for the moment that closes everything. Let 'casa' land with the weight it's earned.

emergency.title: If you are hurt or ill

phrases.es: ¿Me puede ayudar a llamar a alguien?
phrases.en: Can you help me call someone?

phrases.es: No entiendo. Más despacio, por favor.
Lléveme a esta dirección, por favor.
phrases.en: Take me to this address, please.
No thank you. Leave me alone.

phrases.es: Voy a llamar a la policía.
phrases.en: I'm going to call the police.
